description:
Trigger (deterministic mode, the default; no realistic-demo-ids feature):

  let b = MemoryBackend::new().with_account('a');
  let (id1, _) = b.create_object::<Calendar>(&(), &Id::from('a'), 'c1', cal1).await?;  // 'calendar0000000000000001'
  b.destroy_object::<Calendar>(&(), &Id::from('a'), &id1).await?;                       // map now empty, len=0
  let (id2, _) = b.create_object::<Calendar>(&(), &Id::from('a'), 'c2', cal2).await?;  // re-mints 'calendar0000000000000001'

memory.rs:367-371 — demo_next_id computes
  n = inner.objects_ref(type_name, account_id).map_or(0, |m| m.len())
  new_id = format!('{}{:016x}', type_name.to_ascii_lowercase(), n + 1)
After a delete, len() drops, the next create re-uses the destroyed id.

Concrete downstream breakage:
- The change_log keeps the destroyed id in entry K's 'destroyed' AND emits it in entry K+2's 'created'.
- The dedup pass at memory.rs:494-510 sees 'destroyed' second, so a /changes call spanning K..K+2 reports the re-minted id ONLY as destroyed — the create is silently dropped.
- This violates RFC 8620 §5.2 'every distinct state MUST be reported correctly' for clients that calculate state diffs.
- The debug_assert at memory.rs:372-379 does NOT catch this: it fires only when the new id is still in the map, but after destroy it is gone.

This is the same bug fixed in jmap-contacts-server by bd:JMAP-qz9v.14 (commit 0d14538) — a per-(type, account) monotonic counter in Inner.next_ids that only ever increments. The workspace sweep bd:JMAP-h7jp is already open and identifies this crate as in scope.

Fix: mirror contacts-server. Add 'next_ids: HashMap<(&'static str, String), u64>' to Inner; demo_next_id increments and never decrements. Three unit tests from contacts (id_not_recycled_after_destroy, id_namespace_is_per_type_and_account, ids_are_monotonic_within_namespace) should be ported.

P0 because the breakage path is observable from any client doing /changes over a destroy+create round-trip on the same id. Demo-mode is the default mode (no realistic-demo-ids feature on by default), so this affects every test and every consumer who tries the reference impl without enabling the feature.
title: demo_next_id len()-based mode recycles ids after destroy
